prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right one depends on your exact location in Houston, the type/brand/age of your system, whether you need emergency same‑day service, your budget, and whether you want a long warranty or a one‑time repair. I can help you find the best option for your situation — below are practical steps and what to look for so you pick a reliable company.

How to choose the best AC repair company
- Check credentials: confirm the techs are EPA‑608 certified (required to work with refrigerants) and ask about NATE certification (industry quality). Make sure the company is licensed/registered to do HVAC work in Texas and carries liability insurance and workers’ comp.
- Read recent reviews: look at Google, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, and the BBB. Pay attention to recent repair experiences, punctuality, honesty about costs, and warranty follow‑through.
- Get 3 estimates: for non‑emergency repairs, compare at least three written estimates so you can compare diagnostics, parts, labor, and warranties.
- Ask about warranties: get written parts-and-labor warranty terms. Prefer companies that provide at least a 1-year labor warranty on repairs.
- Check specialty and brand experience: if you have a high‑efficiency or less‑common brand, ask whether the company regularly services that make/model and has factory training or parts access.
- Emergency & availability: if you want 24/7 service, confirm emergency response times and after‑hours fees up front.
- Ask for references: especially for larger jobs, ask for recent customer references in your neighborhood.

Questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed and insured in Texas? Can you provide your license/registration number?
- Are your technicians EPA‑608 and NATE certified?
- What is your diagnostic fee, and is that fee applied to the repair if I move forward?
- Do you give a written estimate? What is included (parts, labor, permit, disposal)?
- What warranties do you offer on parts and labor?
- Do you offer flat‑rate pricing or hourly? What is your estimated timeline to complete the job?

Red flags
- No proof of insurance or license
- Huge price differences without itemized breakdowns
- High‑pressure sales tactics to replace the system immediately without clear diagnostics
- No written estimate or warranty

Typical pricing note
- Small diagnostics/repair usually runs from a modest diagnostic fee + parts/labor. Major repairs (compressor, coil, refrigerant leaks) can be several hundred to a few thousand dollars depending on part and labor. Always get written estimates.

Want a short list of local providers?
If you’d like, tell me your Houston ZIP code (and whether it’s residential or commercial, and whether you need same‑day service). I can then suggest several top‑rated local companies and draft a short phone script you can use to vet them.
